notes: Based on the repo's Night tokens and Hearthvale world plan.
Catching is proposed beyond the approved exploration/training implementation slice.
The remote Claude design document was inaccessible; local specifications were used.

screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, detailed product design board for Rental Rumble, a MOBILE-ONLY Pokémon browser game. This is a new set of screens, not an edit of the reference.
Input image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE: faithfully extend its established Night mobile UI. Preserve the dark GBA menu aesthetic, beveled pixel window frames, navy diagonal striped field, crisp authentic Pokémon pixel sprites, luminous pale-blue borders, readable pixel typography, hard shadows, square buttons, warm gold selection cursor and primary action, cyan segmented EXP bars. Palette: field #141a2c, panels #1e2740, rim #8fa6cc, frame #3a4c74, ink #f2f0e6, secondary #9aa6c4, gold #ffd447, blue #7fb4ff, cyan #5fd4ff.
Composition: landscape presentation board, exactly THREE full-height straight-on portrait mobile screen designs in one row, equal width and generous narrow gutters. Each screen is a practical 390×844 mobile layout. No angled phones, no hands, no device hardware, no laptop, no browser chrome. All three screens fully visible, large readable UI text and touch-sized controls, coherent spacing and hierarchy. Detailed pixel environments occupy meaningful screen area, with restrained text and uncluttered thumb-friendly controls. Board title above and short numbered screen captions below. Match the reference's overall presentation and feature-icon language.
All screens have the SAME bottom navigation with five labeled pixel icons: HOME (house), EXPLORE (compass, gold active), PARTY (Poké Ball), DEX (handheld), MENU (three bars). Consistent top bars with back arrow and screen title. NAV stays at bottom, no overlapping panels. Small trainer avatar uses original red cap explorer style. No monetization, ads, energy meters, real maps, desktop sidebars, soft glass, gradients, unreadable lorem ipsum or watermark.
Use actual recognizable Pokémon sprites. Team is Treecko Lv.7, Mareep Lv.6, Poliwag Lv.6 unless the results explicitly evolve/level them. Do not show a full six-member team: three filled slots and three empty ones is purposeful.
Text must be accurately spelled and concise. Product interface, not a marketing poster.
Board title: "NIGHT · INTO THE WORLD". Small subtitle: "Hearthvale · map, destinations, exploration".

LEFT SCREEN — "WORLD MAP".
A beautiful tactile top-down pixel-art region dominates roughly 60% of the screen, hand-crafted GBA environment with winding paths, rivers, wooden bridges, flowers, forest, distant mountain, quarry and ancient ruins. Hearth Town is a small cozy cluster of red roofs at lower left, SUNNY MEADOW a golden sunlit grass route in the middle with current trainer marker. MOSSY WOODS farther north has a lock icon and labeled path. Distant biome areas hide under patterned fog with "???" markers. No floating generic map pins; use little in-world signs and tactile pixel landmark nodes linked by walking trails. Header "HEARTHVALE", sublabel "1 / 6 routes discovered", right small list icon. Map zoom + / – and recenter buttons. On map labels "Hearth Town", "Sunny Meadow", "Mossy Woods". Show tiny lock/key state legend by the map edge.
A bottom summary window below the map: folded green map icon, "SUNNY MEADOW", "Meadow · Rec. Lv.3–8", tiny Treecko/Mareep/Poliwag portraits, and gold full-width primary "VIEW LOCATION". Small secondary hint "Drag to pan · Tap a place". Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "01 / WORLD MAP".

MIDDLE SCREEN — "SUNNY MEADOW".
A scenic 35%-height pixel meadow panorama with tall golden-green grass, a flower-lined stream, hilltop oak, Sentret and Pidgey sightings, daytime clouds. A compact back/title row above. Content bottom sheet is built from Night pixel windows, never white.
Location detail header "ROUTE 1 · SUNNY MEADOW"; blue small chip "MEADOW" and "REC. LV.3–8".
Progress row: eye icon "6 / 9 seen", journal icon "1 / 3 landmarks", three mastery pips labelled "CLEAR · SURVEY · CATALOGUE", only Survey partial rather than falsely completed.
"LOCAL POKÉMON" strip of 5 small sprites including Sentret, Pidgey, Hoppip, Bidoof, and a mysterious Eevee silhouette with a tiny gold rare sparkle.
Guardian row shows Furret portrait: "GUARDIAN · FURRET LV.7"; smaller "Defeat to open Mossy Woods".
Compact "YOUR PARTY" tray: Treecko Lv.7, Mareep Lv.6, Poliwag Lv.6, three empty slots, edit arrow.
Two very clear activities: big gold "EXPLORE" with little boots icon and smaller caption "Choose your path"; dark framed "TRAIN HERE" with cyan EXP icon and caption "6 EXP / win · 4 min / battle". Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "02 / CHOOSE AN ADVENTURE".

RIGHT SCREEN — "ON THE TRAIL".
Top "SUNNY MEADOW", below "CHECKPOINT 2 / 5" with five connected pips, first filled gold, second outlined gold, three muted. Main middle scene is a close top-down pixel overworld: tiny red-cap adult trainer walking with Treecko and two companions behind, a signpost at an actual fork. One path heads into tall rustling grass with sparkle hint; another toward a tranquil hilltop oak. Warm sunlight, layered trees, little rocks, readable path geometry; a feeling of being inside the world.
Floating tiny discovery note "Old Signpost discovered" with field journal icon.
Lower Night window title "A FORK IN THE PATH", copy "The grass rustles. Which way?"
Two stacked touch-sized choices: "▶ TALL GRASS" / "Tougher battles · Rare sightings", and "MEADOW PATH" / "Calmer trail · Hilltop Oak".
Bottom compact footer above nav: cyan EXP symbol "20 EXP banked" and secondary "RETREAT". Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "03 / EXPLORE THE ROUTE".

Board title: "NIGHT · CATCH, TRAIN & GROW". Small subtitle: "Mobile screen concepts · catching is a proposed extension".

LEFT SCREEN — "A WILD ENCOUNTER".
Top back/title "SUNNY MEADOW", small "RARE ENCOUNTER". A cinematic but distinctly pixel-art battle-clearing scene occupies upper half: an adorable authentic Eevee pixel sprite facing the viewer in sunlit tall grass, flowers, a stream and leafy trees, a few restrained sparkles. Eevee stays identifiable and proportional, not enlarged into a realistic illustration. Large framed identity plaque "EEVEE · LV.5" and a brown type label "NORMAL". Small field notebook status "NEW SIGHTING".
Below scene a Night dialogue box: "Eevee is watching you..." Small label "CATCH OPPORTUNITY".
Ball selection is tangible illustrated pixel item tiles, not a slot machine: selected gold-framed Poké Ball tile "POKÉ BALL ×12", neighboring Great Ball tile "GREAT BALL ×3", berry tile "BERRY ×4". Each is readable and large enough to tap.
A wide gold button with ball icon "THROW POKÉ BALL". Beneath it two secondary buttons "OBSERVE" and "LET IT GO".
Small strip "YOUR LEAD" with Treecko portrait "Treecko · Lv.7", segmented HP bar, and switch arrow. Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "04 / CATCH A NEW COMPANION".
Do not add exact catch percentages, gambling visuals, swipe aiming overlays, or pretend this mechanic is already implemented.

MIDDLE SCREEN — "TRAINING".
Header "TRAINING AT SUNNY MEADOW", small cyan label "PARTY OUT TRAINING".
A large charming side-view pixel landscape: red-cap adult trainer with Treecko, Mareep and Poliwag travelling along a sunlit meadow route, tall grass, hilltop oak, Pidgey on fence. This should communicate an active expedition continuing while the player is away.
A framed time panel displays "2h 13m / 8h" and a cyan segmented elapsed bar filled a little over one quarter. Smaller "Next battle in 3m". Metric pair: "33 WINS" and "+198 EXP EACH". Small status "Training stops at the first defeat".
Below: three horizontal party rows with portraits, names and CURRENT levels: "TREECKO · LV.7", "MAREEP · LV.6", "POLIWAG · LV.6". Each has cyan "+198 EXP pending"; levels do not change before returning. Calm note "EXP is applied when you return".
Primary gold "RETURN & COLLECT", secondary "KEEP TRAINING". Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "05 / TRAIN WHILE AWAY".

RIGHT SCREEN — "TRAINING COMPLETE".
A celebratory but restrained result screen, heading "BACK FROM THE MEADOW" and small trophy icon "33 BATTLES WON".
Hero reward window with large crisp Treecko sprite, gold arrow, recognizable Grovyle sprite and a few pixel sparkles, title "TREECKO EVOLVED!", subtitle "GROVYLE · LV.8".
Three reward rows each with sprite, old → new level and cyan EXP:
"GROVYLE  LV.7 → 8" / "+198 EXP";
"MAREEP  LV.6 → 7" / "+198 EXP";
"POLIWAG  LV.6 → 7" / "+198 EXP".
Use clear segmented cyan progress bars for each. The first row's name Grovyle reflects final species. This game intentionally evolves starters at level 8, so Grovyle at 8 is correct.
Small discovery window with journal icon "NEW SIGHTINGS", two tiny recognizable sprites "Pidgey" and "Hoppip". No route unlock reward from training, since only exploration guardians unlock places.
Wide gold "BACK TO WORLD MAP"; secondary dark button "TRAIN AGAIN". Bottom navigation.
Caption beneath: "06 / LEVEL UP & EVOLVE".
